findings.title: Optional success_statuses handled with `or`, not an explicit None check
findings.problem: `success_statuses: set[int] | None = None` is folded into a default via `success_statuses or {200, 201}`. Because `or` treats any falsy value as absent, a caller that explicitly passes an empty set (e.g. to express 'no status code should be treated as success') would silently get the default {200, 201} instead.
findings.fix_hint: use `success_statuses if success_statuses is not None else {200, 201}` so only the None sentinel triggers the default
findings.why_it_matters: The two current call sites never hit this, so it's latent rather than active today, but it silently masks caller intent for any future caller that passes an empty set, and it's the kind of Optional-handling bug that's easy to miss in review since the code 'looks' like it already guards None.

members.title: Cancel failures raise TransferEnqueueError, so handlers written for enqueue failures will catch them
members.problem: _request_json is now shared by the DELETE cancel path, but every non-auth failure still raises TransferEnqueueError. pipeline.py:924 has an `except TransferEnqueueError` that rewraps errors as enqueue failures. If cancel_download is ever called inside a block like that, a failed cancel would be reported as a failed enqueue or poll. pending: confirm whether the planned cancel call site sits inside an enqueue/poll `except TransferEnqueueError` handler.
